nodes.name: Precursor formation
nodes.procedure: 1.58 g of benzimidazole, 1.5 ml of aniline and 5 kinds of transition metal salts in the appropriate proportions (2 g Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 1.37 g Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 1.37 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.63 g MnCl2 and 1.1 g Cu(NO3)2·3H2O) were added to 200 ml of 1.5 M hydrochloric acid solution under magnetic stirring for 30 min at room temperature. Then, 0.88 g ammonium persulfate and 0.2 g Ketjen Black were added to this solution. The mixture was then magnetically stirred for another four hours before the suspension was collected and washed by suction filtration using deionized water and then dried at 60 °C in a vacuum oven overnight. The resulting solid was the HESA precursor.
nodes.source_text: First, 1.58 of benzimidazole, 1.5 ml of aniline and 5 kinds of transition metal salts... The resulting solid was the HESA precursor.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis and acid leaching
nodes.procedure: The collected black-green powders were pyrolysed under Ar at 900 °C for one hour with a rate of temperature rise of 10 °C min⁻¹ before being allowed to cool naturally to room temperature. The powders were then pickled in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ at 80 °C for 8 h to remove residual oxides and metal particles, then suction filtered and cleaned before being left to dry overnight.
nodes.source_text: The collected black-green powders were pyrolysed under Ar at 900 °C... left to dry overnight.

nodes.name: Nitrogen doping annealing
nodes.procedure: Finally, secondary heat treatment under Ar was performed, during which a porcelain boat containing melamine was placed around the sample. The sample was first heated to 550 °C for 2 h, followed by annealing at 900 °C for 3 h. Finally, the product was collected and ground to powder.

nodes.description: ORR performance in O₂-saturated 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The ORR activity of the NC, Fe-SA and HESA catalysts was evaluated in O₂-saturated 0.1 M KOH using the rotating disk electrode technique... HESA shows the best performance, with an E_onset of 0.96 V and an E_1/2 of 0.87 V... Tafel slope of HESA (81.9 mV dec⁻¹)... after 1,000 cycles... half-wave potential dropped only 5 mV... current density of HESA remains 97% after... 12 h

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows rough and porous surface of HESA on micrometre scale.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Supplementary Fig. 6 shows the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image of the as-obtained HESA on a micrometre scale, displaying a rough and porous surface

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals nanostructure with packed roughly spherical carbon particles 40–60 nm in diameter and no metal clusters observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution SEM image (Fig. 3b) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Fig. 3c and Supplementary Fig. 7) reveal a nanostructure with packed roughly spherical carbon, 40–60 nm in diameter (Fig. 3e), and no metal clusters were observed

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF–STEM shows bright spots corresponding to Mn, Fe, Co, Ni and Cu single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Mn, Fe, Co, Ni and Cu atoms appear as bright spots in the aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF–STEM) images (Fig. 3f)

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirms uniform distribution of N, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni and Cu across the carbon substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy of HESA in Fig. 3f and Supplementary Fig. 8 corroborates the uniform distribution of N, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni and Cu across the surface of the carbon substrate

nodes.characterization_summary: HESA BET surface area 835.7 m² g⁻¹ with pore size ~5.1 nm, pore volume 1.98 cm³ g⁻¹; Fe-SA 780.5 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A Brunauer–Emmett–Teller analysis reveals that HESA has a larger surface area (835.7 m² g⁻¹) with a pore-size distribution of around 5.1 nm in diameter and 1.98 cm³ g⁻¹ in volume than Fe-SA counterpart (780.5 m² g⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: HESA metal contents: Mn 0.43 wt%, Fe 0.93 wt%, Co 0.36 wt%, Ni 0.41 wt%, Cu 0.67 wt%; Fe-SA: Fe 0.94 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass loading of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni and Cu on the HESA was determined by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP–OES) to be 0.43, 0.93, 0.36, 0.41 and 0.67 wt%, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Thermogravimetric analysis shows excellent thermal stability with onset decomposition temperature Td = 410°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We also carried out thermogravimetric analysis of the HESA and control samples. The results showed that these carbon-based materials have excellent thermal stability (onset decomposition temperature, Td = 410°C, Supplementary Fig. 10)

nodes.characterization_summary: Broad shoulder peak at 2θ 20-30° from graphitic carbon (002) and weak peak at 45° (100); no metal, alloy or carbide peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction patterns of the NC, Fe-SA and HESA catalysts show only a broad shoulder peak at 2θ of 20-30° generated from the graphitic carbon (002) lattice plane and a weak peak at 45° corresponding to the (100) plane

nodes.characterization_summary: D band at 1332 cm⁻¹ and G band at 1580 cm⁻¹; ID/IG ratios 1.14 for HESA, indicating graphitic carbon with rich defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Supplementary Fig. 12a) further demonstrate that the carbon in all three samples is present in a similar form of graphitic carbon with rich defects, as they showed obvious characteristic peaks of the D band (1332 cm⁻¹)... and the ID/IG ratio for these samples is 1.13, 1.09 and 1.14, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 3459 cm⁻¹ (N-H stretch), 1580 cm⁻¹ (N-H bend), 1198 cm⁻¹ (C-N stretch) confirm amino-modification.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR–FTIR) spectra also display the same peak at 3459 cm⁻¹ that corresponds to the N–H stretching vibration of NH₂... and the peaks at 1580 and 1198 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to the N–H bending vibration and C–N stretching vibration, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows Fe valence +2.30 in HESA (+2.25 in Fe-SA); pre-edge peaks at ~7113.5 eV indicate Fe–N₄ coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe K-edge XANES spectra of Fe-SA and Fe-HESA show that these materials have different near-edge absorptions from those of Fe foil, FeO and Fe₂O₃ (Fig. 4a), and the valence states of Fe in Fe-SA and Fe-HESA are +2.25 and +2.30, respectively (Fig. 4b). ... The pre-edge peaks of Fe-SA and Fe-HESA at ~7,113.5 eV were ascribed to the 1s–4pz transitions, suggesting the presence of Fe–N₄ coordination

nodes.characterization_summary: FT EXAFS shows single Fe-N peak at ~1.57 Å; no Fe-Fe peaks, confirming atomic dispersion of metals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the k²-weighted Fourier transformed (FT) EXAFS spectra demonstrate that Fe-SA and HESA display only a single peak at ~1.57 Å attributed to the Fe–N scattering path, while the Fe foil shows a dominant peak at ~2.2 Å
